brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Build has 2 adjacent cells (piece:0,0,0;full + piece:1,0,0;full) each with a full-depth bin (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full) providing two open containers; dressed with fork/spoon props to show utensil use.

Configurator verifies geometry/mesh only; parts are 3D-printed in user-chosen material. Waterproofing depends on material, print sealing and layer adhesion which cannot be verified here. Shape provides two bin trays but no guaranteed watertight performance.

Dishwasher safety depends on material heat resistance, food-safety certification and print process, none of which the configurator checks. No material/process claim can be made. User must choose a dishwasher-safe, food-safe material and validate independently.

finish.summary: Built linear 2-bin holder (two full-depth bins on joint-bolted base). Waterproof/dishwasher-safe cannot be met by configurator – requires material selection outside system scope.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
